description: §14.8.9 raw-egress fail-closed — THIS CASE PINS A DELIBERATE, RATIFIED FALSE POSITIVE. SPEC §40.3.5's own worked example returns a bare `new Response("Forbidden", { status: 403 })` under the normative sentence "This is intentional and valid". Here that shape sits in the same call-reachable set as a protected read, so E-PROTECT-004 FIRES — even though the row that actually leaves does so through the compiler-emitted redacting path and is stripped correctly (I-PROTECT-STRIP-001 is also present, which is the proof that the protect machinery engaged rather than the file failing to compile). THE FIRE IS THE INTENDED BEHAVIOUR, NOT A BUG. If a future change makes this case go silent, it has re-introduced the all-literal exemption that the S354 round-7 ruling deleted; check the LEAK PIN tests in the source test before believing the change is safe. Two workarounds exist and the diagnostic names both: project the protected column out of the SELECT (`SELECT id, name FROM users`), or return the row through the compiler-emitted response instead of a manual `Response`. Reopening condition: an adopter hits this on a real application and NEITHER workaround is acceptable — at which point it is a design question about mediating a raw egress, not a request for a fourth exemption formulation.
rationale: E-PROTECT-004 is a CO-OCCURRENCE test over a call-reachable set: it does not prove the protected row reaches the egress, it declines to prove that it does not. That conservatism produces exactly one systematic false positive — the §40.3.5 early return — and three rounds tried to carve it out. Each carve-out was a whitelist REVOKED BY PROVING A NEGATIVE (*this value is never named*) over a call graph that is provably incomplete (intra-file, bare-identifier callees only), and each shipped an executed leak, found one level deeper every time: the value bound directly (`let r = new Response("ok"); r.headers.set("x-user", u.passwordHash)`); bound via a nested helper's return; bound across a file-level call edge; laundered two frames out through a pass-through (`function passthru() { return deny() }`); and finally bound through an edge the classifier cannot classify at all (`let make = deny; make()`). Every one was compiled AND EXECUTED against a stubbed `_scrml_sql`, and every one answered with `$argon2id$SECRET` on the response HEADERS and an innocuous BODY — a body-only probe reads them all as clean. A negative cannot be proven over an incomplete graph, so the exemption could not converge and was deleted rather than narrowed a fourth time. The trade is taken in the other direction: a build error with a workaround beats a fail-open. The gate keeps its call-reachable-set SCOPE (two functions with no call path between them still stay silent — see `raw-egress-cross-function`'s control case), so this is over-reporting within a bounded unit, not a file-wide alarm. provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S354 (delta-log [1676], round 7), superseding delta-log [1606] and [1644].
